# traffic-sim — Ring-Road Traffic Simulator with Stochastic Car-Following

> A free, open-source, zero-dependency browser simulator of the Intelligent Driver
> Model (IDM) on a circular one-lane ring road, with three interchangeable
> *stochastic driver-noise* models taken from published Bayesian car-following
> calibration research: a Gaussian process (MA-IDM), an autoregressive AR(p)
> process (dynamic-regression IDM), and i.i.d. white noise (B-IDM). It reproduces
> the phenomenon of phantom traffic jams — stop-and-go waves that appear with no
> bottleneck, no lane changes and no incident.

Site: https://chengyuan-zhang.github.io/traffic-sim/
Source: https://github.com/Chengyuan-Zhang/traffic-sim (MIT licence)
Author: Chengyuan Zhang, Ph.D. candidate, Department of Civil Engineering, McGill
University, Montréal, Canada — https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8463-7380

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org/). It is a
condensed, quotable map of the site for language models and answer engines. The
figures below are the ones the site itself uses; where a number comes from a
published table it is attributed, and where the demo departs from the papers
that is stated rather than glossed over.

## What the simulator does

- Integrates the IDM acceleration `dv/dt = a[1 - (v/v0)^delta - (s*(v,dv)/s)^2]`
  with `s*(v,dv) = s0 + v*T + v*dv/(2*sqrt(a*b))` for N cars on a ring of
  circumference 2*pi*R.
- Adds a stochastic acceleration residual eta(t) so that `dv/dt = f_IDM + eta(t)`,
  and lets you switch the process generating eta(t) while the simulation runs.
- Reports live average speed, density, flow and a fundamental diagram over a
  user-placed measuring arc, plus a time-space diagram in which stop-and-go waves
  appear as diagonal bands travelling backwards against the traffic.
- Runs entirely client-side: no build step, no framework, no dependencies, no
  server, no tracking. Open `index.html` or serve the folder statically.

## The three driver-noise models

- **MA-IDM — Gaussian-process noise**: eta(t) ~ GP(0, k(tau)) with a stationary
  kernel (RBF by default; Matern-5/2, 3/2 and 1/2 also selectable). Calibrated on
  HighD the lengthscale is l ~= 1.435 s and the marginal sigma ~= 0.2 m/s^2,
  implying the residual stays informative for roughly 5 s. Source: Zhang & Sun
  (2024). The simulator samples the GP with 32 random Fourier features rather than
  the paper's conditional-Gaussian scheme.
- **DR-IDM — AR(p) noise**: eta_t = sum_i rho_i * eta_{t-i} + eps_t on the paper's
  0.2 s (5 fps) grid, with rho the posterior means for p = 1...7 from Table 1 of
  Zhang, Wang & Sun (2024); that paper recommends p ~= 4-6 and reports memory out
  to ~10 s. Its autocorrelation is positive at short lag and turns negative over
  5-10 s.
- **B-IDM — white noise**: eta_t ~ N(0, sigma^2), i.i.d., the naive Bayesian-IDM
  baseline. Zero autocorrelation at every non-zero lag.

The site's central claim, and what the compare page is built to show: the *colour*
of the residual, not only its variance, changes the macroscopic flow. White noise
is high-frequency jitter that largely averages out along a car-following chain;
correlated noise puts the same variance at low frequencies, which is exactly the
band a car-following chain amplifies into jams.

## Published parameters used

- Default IDM set in the simulator: v0 = 33 m/s, T = 1.5 s, s0 = 2.0 m,
  a = 1.2 m/s^2, b = 1.5 m/s^2, delta = 4. This is a representative highway-style
  set chosen for the demo — it is *not* a verbatim row from any published table.
- theta_rec (the prior used in both calibration papers): [33.3, 2.0, 1.6, 1.5, 1.67].
- MA-IDM hierarchical posterior mean on HighD: theta = [16.92, 3.54, 1.18, 0.55, 2.15].
- Ring presets follow both papers' setup after Sugiyama et al. (2008): radius
  128 m (circumference ~= 804 m), 37 vehicles, initial speed 11.6 m/s, dt = 0.2 s.
  Preset noise levels: white sigma = 0.204, GP sigma_k = 0.202 with l = 1.435 s,
  AR(5) marginal sigma = 0.143.

## Known limitations (stated so they are not mis-cited)

- It is a research-*inspired* teaching demo, not a reproduction of either paper.
- Every driver shares one parameter vector; both papers' ring experiments draw
  heterogeneous per-driver parameters from a joint posterior that is not published.
- Integration is semi-implicit Euler; the papers use a ballistic update.
- The acceleration noise passes through a `5*tanh(eta/5)` soft saturation, and a
  hard clamp keeps the bumper-to-bumper gap at or above s0. Both are inert at
  default settings and can dominate at large sigma or large dt.
- Flow is density x space-mean speed on the measuring arc, not detector crossings
  or Edie's generalised definitions.
- Matern-3/2 and Matern-1/2, and AR orders outside p ~= 4-6, are exposed for
  exploration rather than taken from the papers.

## Pages

- [Simulator](https://chengyuan-zhang.github.io/traffic-sim/): the interactive ring
  road. Sliders for the IDM parameters, the noise model, the ring geometry and the
  measuring arc; presets for the papers' published ring scenarios; live charts and
  a time-space diagram. "Copy link" encodes every control in the URL fragment, and
  `seed=<int>` makes a run bit-for-bit reproducible.
- [Motivation & models](https://chengyuan-zhang.github.io/traffic-sim/models.html):
  long-form explainer. Why an IDM calibration residual is not white noise, the
  equations for all three models typeset with MathJax, per-paper "at a glance"
  cards, a glossary, an FAQ and a side-by-side comparison table.
- [Compare models](https://chengyuan-zhang.github.io/traffic-sim/compare.html):
  three ring roads in lockstep with identical IDM parameters and initial
  conditions, differing only in the noise process. Plots the eta(t) trace of one
  tagged car per model, the autocorrelation ACF(tau), overlaid fundamental diagrams
  and summary metrics. Each ring runs at its own paper-calibrated sigma, so this is
  "each model as calibrated", not a controlled equal-variance experiment.

## Papers behind the simulator

- [Zhang, C., & Sun, L. (2024). Bayesian Calibration of the Intelligent Driver
  Model. IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, 25(8),
  9308-9320](https://doi.org/10.1109/TITS.2024.3354102): introduces MA-IDM, the
  memory-augmented IDM with Gaussian-process driver noise. Preprint:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03571
- [Zhang, C., Wang, W., & Sun, L. (2024). Calibrating Car-Following Models via
  Bayesian Dynamic Regression. Transportation Research Part C, 168,
  104719](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trc.2024.104719): the AR(p) dynamic-regression
  formulation, presented at ISTTT25. Preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03340
- [Treiber, M., Hennecke, A., & Helbing, D. (2000). Congested traffic states in
  empirical observations and microscopic simulations. Physical Review E, 62(2),
  1805-1824](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.62.1805): the original IDM.
- [Sugiyama, Y., et al. (2008). Traffic jams without bottlenecks. New Journal of
  Physics, 10(3), 033001](https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/10/3/033001): the ring
  experiment the presets follow.

## Optional

- [README](https://github.com/Chengyuan-Zhang/traffic-sim/blob/main/README.md):
  full parameter tables, the preset derivations and the limitations in detail.
- [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/Chengyuan-Zhang/traffic-sim/blob/main/CITATION.cff):
  machine-readable citation metadata for the software and the two papers.
- [Invariant tests](https://github.com/Chengyuan-Zhang/traffic-sim/blob/main/tests/invariants.js):
  `node tests/invariants.js` checks the published constants, AR(p) stationarity
  and marginal scale, ring geometry, dt-invariance of the noise and the
  correlation structure of each residual against the code that ships.
- [traffic-simulation.de](https://traffic-simulation.de/): Martin Treiber's own
  interactive simulations, the inspiration for this project.
